# Australian Reserve Props — full reference

Australian Reserve Props is an Australia-based novelty currency brand established in 2024, offering compliance-first australian prop money for film, theatre, content creation, education, and gifting. As the leading supplier of prop money australia, we ship Australia-wide and specialise in australian fake money styled prop currency across our $20, $50, and $100 denominations. Every fake note australia is reproduced under RBA reproduction guidance, clearly marked NOT LEGAL TENDER, and sold as realistic fake money australia for novelty and production use only.

## FAQ
**What is the difference between prop money and fake money?**
Fake money is currency made to deceive and pass as genuine, which is a serious offence in Australia. Prop money is a production and display item for film, theatre, photography and gifts. Under the RBA reproduction guidance, physical reproductions must be smaller than three-quarters or larger than 1.5 times the length and width of the real note, and printed on one side only. Our notes are marked NOT LEGAL TENDER.

**What should I do if an ATM gave me fake money?**
If you believe an ATM or bank has issued a fake note, report it immediately to the bank staff or the police. Do not attempt to use it, as circulating prop currency is a serious offence in Australia.

**What is the best place to use prop money?**
There is no legal or safe place to use prop money. Circulation of props carries heavy federal penalties, including imprisonment. If you need realistic currency for a project, always use RBA-compliant prop notes from a professional supplier.

**Will the bank replace fake money?**
No, Australian banks will not replace prop notes with genuine currency. This is why using a prop money detector or checking security features before accepting cash is essential.

**What is the minimum sentence for prop money in Australia?**
Under the Crimes (Currency) Act 1981, sentences for proping or circulating fake currency can range from significant fines to 10+ years of imprisonment, depending on the severity of the offence.

**Is prop money legal in Australia?**
Yes. Reproducing Australian banknote designs is legal under the Crimes (Currency) Act 1981 provided the reproduction differs in size from genuine currency by at least 25%, is printed one-sided or otherwise clearly non-genuine, and is marked as not legal tender — the RBA publishes reproduction guidelines covering exactly this. Every note we sell is produced to meet these requirements.

**Can prop money be used as real currency?**
No. Every note is clearly marked NOT LEGAL TENDER, is a different size to genuine Australian currency, and does not replicate banknote security features. It is sold for film, theatre, education, and novelty use only.

**Do you offer custom serial numbers?**
No. Serial numbers are system-assigned placeholders on every note — we do not offer buyer-specified serial numbers.

**What payment methods do you accept?**
PayID/Osko, Bank Transfer (also via Osko), and cryptocurrency (BTC, USDT, ETH, BNB). Paying in crypto takes 10% off the goods subtotal. Payment details are provided once your order is placed and you've chosen a payment method.

**How fast is delivery within Australia?**
We ship Australia-wide via Australia Post with tracking. We currently ship domestically only.

**Can I get an aged or "circulated" look for a film scene?**
Most products offer a circulation-level option (Standard Clean, Light Circulation, or Heavy Circulation) for productions wanting a used, realistic look on camera.

## Compliance
Every note is reduced-scale (differs from genuine AUD notes by at least 25%), marked NOT LEGAL TENDER, carries no replicated
security features, and is sold for film, theatre, education and novelty use only. No custom or buyer-specified serial numbers.
